classification.difficultyReason: Apply the same horizontal substitution to both numerator and denominator, then preserve both branches and asymptotes.

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, question 32, between introductory sentence and sketch instruction
spec.description: Two rational-function branches with continuation arrows; dashed horizontal asymptote labelled 3/2 and vertical asymptote labelled 1/2.

answer.short:
Translate 1 unit right. The asymptotes are $x=\frac32$ and $y=\frac32$.

Replace $x$ with $x-1$ in both the numerator and denominator.
answer.worked:
Replace $x$ with $x-1$ throughout the original rule.
$$\begin{align*}y&=\frac{3(x-1)+1}{2(x-1)-1}\\y&=\frac{3x-2}{2x-3}\end{align*}$$
Translate both branches 1 unit right. The vertical asymptote moves from $x=\frac12$ to $x=\frac32$; the horizontal asymptote remains $y=\frac32$. The right branch remains above the horizontal asymptote and the left branch remains below it.
